baseline: eslint-config-next 16.4.3 core-web-vitals + typescript; effective rules for current TSX sources
policy: ESLint 10.14.0 and every installed plugin have compatible peer ranges. No force or legacy-peer-deps is used.

npm run lint includes tsc --noEmit --incremental false. All JSX must live in TSX; JSX in JS/JSX/MJS/CJS is rejected. checkJs remains false, so TypeScript is not claimed to validate ordinary JavaScript.
React class components and external create-react-class factories are conservatively rejected. The current application uses function components; no application code changed.
Both warnings and errors fail the lint gate because --max-warnings is zero.

The maintained import-x package exposes a supported rule subpath. Only the previously enabled no-anonymous-default-export rule is imported; unrelated glob rules with an incompatible minimatch makeRe API are not loaded.

unchanged.@next/next: All recommended + core-web-vitals rules from @next/eslint-plugin-next 16.4.3, with the existing native-image exception for the two product-image components.
unchanged.react-hooks: All recommended rules from eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.1.1, unchanged from the resolved baseline.
unchanged.@typescript-eslint: All recommended rules from typescript-eslint 8.67.0; no-unused-vars and no-unused-expressions remain warnings, all other previous severities retained.

deprecationNotes: All top-level APIs from the old no-deprecated rule are retained. Entire removed React.addons/PropTypes namespaces and all class components are conservatively rejected, covering their old nested/lifecycle checks. React.createFactory is also rejected for React 19. transferPropsTo is rejected on every object. Context.displayName was not enabled by the old display-name rule and is not newly required.
